t:
Further information was not preserved in written form, but you received a vision that allowed you to learn about the ending of the story.

"A kaleidoscope of images whirl through your mind as you touch this artifact: the Junes, fighting a thousand bloody battles with dragons. The losses on both sides are huge, but the hatred burns so hot that no one cares to stop. One after another, the Great Dragons, Keepers of the Prison, fall before the growing power. The first among the dragon hunters is Tka-Rik, the greatest mage that Sarnaut has ever seen.

Finally, eight of the Great Dragons are dead. There's only one left. He's hiding in the mountains like a coward. It won't be long until he's killed, and the Junes fulfill their pledge. But the night comes when the darkness thickens and turns into a monster that has no name. The dismayed Junes face it in the ancient city near the source of celestial iron."

One more translation of another part of this story:

"And then the Dark One, as the Junes call him, spoke to them:

He said, "Oh, the Junes! Sarn told you to kill all dragons. Did he tell you what awaits you afterwards?"

The Junes were confused. They didn't know how to reply.

"You see, the very second you kill the last dragon, this world will cease to exist. Of course, Sarn will be set free. But you all are going to die!"

The Junes then asked what the Dark One was suggesting.

"I will give you the choice that Sarn didn't offer you. You may choose to keep the promise you gave Sarn, and die together with Sarnaut. Or you could forget about the dragon hunt!"

The Junes then asked if Nihaz could protect them from Sarn's wrath.

"I don't fear Sarn! Behold the Star Gates through which I travel between the worlds... Should there be danger, I will give you a new world, and you'll be your own masters!"
The Junes then renounced their promise. They gave their answer to the Dark One in the place where the magic power of the world spilled and transformed into thousands of elementals. This is where the June Curse was born!"

Nihaz summed it up in the end:

"Hah, I hope you realize now that the Junes' fate was their own fault?

Their success depended on the dragon blood, the borrowed power that failed to help them against the Curse of their own Creator.

The Great Mage Tka-Rik? What a whiner. After everything that happened to the Junes, he blamed himself, felt remorse, and condemned himself to centuries of imprisonment under Gipat mountains. But his legacy survived. The elves have awakened to find a lot of Junes' artifacts, including those of blood magic. It ended badly for them. With time, they hit upon the idea of trying dragon blood.

This is how they got their own Great Mages, who later trained Skrakan, who then trained the others, and finally, you all nearly destroyed the world by shattering it into pieces.

Thank Tka-Rik and his thirst for revenge for all this."

You had to find the last Spark that belonged to Ath-Zak. This is how Nihaz instructed you before you left for the Coba Plateau:

"The time has come for our final game in these lands.

If you only knew how hard it is to stage Performances for you! Actors never stick to the script, prop masters damage the props...

I had to put in a lot of effort to stage a small Performance for someone whose Spark you're going to be looking for. Starting a rumor on Suslanger that there are meteorites in the Futile Lands... Whispering to Kanian descendants on Gipat that the Chosen One will appear in the old ruins. And finally, send the weakened Curse after the last Junes...

Ath-Zak's Spark wasn't all that valuable for me after all. A crafty thief once stole it. I won't tell you when it happened or who he was, but here's a generous hint. This is a fragment of the letter he wrote when he left for the Coba Plateau..."

I won't describe your pursuit of one unlucky Gibberling. I will only tell you about some of the visions you had, and will attach the relevant documents.

So here are the visions you had near the stone arch:

"Everything is so hazy... You see a different place... but you realize that it's the Coba Plateau, only thousands of years ago. You see a thin man in white robes. Only his amber eyes can be seen under the mask. He leans over a June stele to read the text on it. He's silent and thoughtful.

You hear someone calling "Tep!", and the man turns around."

"Everything is blurry and sparkly. You can see consequences of a terrible war that happened in this land. Traces of battles, dead bodies... no living thing dares to approach the bodies. There are no vultures or scavengers here. The "non-life" seems to be caused by an unknown disease that killed everything.

Suddenly you see a girl with light ginger hair and delicate features. She walks between the bodies. Waves of the black disease are rolling away from her.

"You can do it," she says to herself and raises her hands to cast a powerful spell. "You are the soul of the world."

Here are some interesting documents you found on a pirate ship:

"You're reading a page from the folder. It's titled, "Marianna Lopatina's Log, August 13, 1018"

This is the last page of my log. Goblins stole the other pages. There's something wrong in the Holy Lands. Now I'm thinking about coincidences. The legend of Ath-Zak is called "Cursed Lands".

Are the Holy and the Cursed Lands all that different? When the world wasn't split apart, it took only a few days to get from Gipat to Eljune.

Now it's time to sum up my travel. Junes' fate is clear. They fell under the Curse that has been hunting for the Junes. They separated. Some of them became Wormfaces, others managed to escape.

The outcasts are now condemned to misery. I spoke with a Tep's Cultist. He was kind enough to share some information after I threatened to blast him apart.

Tep took great interest in the Junes' legacy. He and his servants met the Junes who escaped from the Curse. There were rumors about a city in the mountains under a spell so powerful that it drove the Curse away.

This city was where Gipat is now. Was it Tka-Rik's farewell gift? We can only guess the future. Hundreds of years later, the Aro tribes came to these lands. They formed an alliance with the June descendants which gave the world many talented creators.

My readers probably have already guessed what it is. Today it is known as the Dead City. Nothing lasts forever. The Curse was destined to find June descendants sooner or later. Some of them escaped again. More Kanians than Junes, they now live in the Village.

When Zak came to the Village, he found his distant relatives. Is this Fate mocking us? It's up to you to decide.

I'm going on a new expedition. I want to find out if Jigran is a legend or reality."

"You're reading another page from the folder. It's titled "Noel de Blizare's Journal". Here's a fragment:

I never regretted going on this expedition!

It's what my teacher, the famous naturalist Alphonse de Ardeur, would have wanted.

The Holy Lands are full of various life forms. I talked to almost all of them! It makes you think: what could one discuss with a troll? How to approach a Mantis? What could Harpies tell you?

I'll tell you - there's a way to everyone's heart. For instance, I talked to ogres. They are considered rude and cruel, and unjustly so! There's beauty in everyone. It may be too deep, But it's important to find the right words.

I managed. It turns out, the poor primitive minds can easily be influenced, if you just keep talking... But not everyone is capable of it. I'm remembering poor Adele de Grandeur... She had a brilliant mind and several PhDs, but she faltered and stammered... and became an ogre's meal.

What's also important is these people are preserving their history. They write songs and poems, carve pictures on bones. I've learned a lot. The ancient legends from the June times, stories about wars of the past...

The Junes were belligerent. With the education they received from our Elven ancestors, they became a truly fearsome power. They built Paths that allowed them to navigate the portal network. We've only recently started to figure them out! Not to mention golems, both small and big as a mountain!

Lamias, for example, remember the June wars very well. Alphonse was right about them. Lamias worshipped a snake goddess. Junes found her and slayed her. Fancy that - they killed a real albeit minor deity! No wonder the dragons weren't a problem for them.

I'm sending my notes to Bertille de Pluie. She's smart - maybe she could put them all together in a book.

Bertille's handwritten note: "Someone explain to this fool that "personal contact" does not mean what she thinks it means."

"You're reading another page from the folder. "A letter from Yaver Amenia, Evette de Doucer, and Antoinette de Grandeur to the Council of Historians on allod Neigh." Here's a fragment:

Dear colleagues, we have completed the study of the June ruins on Eljune. In the course of our research, we reconstructed the history of this location.

June Itsmal was one of the largest June cities. Located in the bay, it had an exit to the open sea and the ocean surrounding Yule. This made it a major trade port. The city comprised not only the immediate area of today's June Itsmal, but also the vast area from the Jakala Ruins to the Icemirror Lake.

Goods from all over the world were brought to the city. There is evidence that trade was conducted with Tekyan people from Irdrich and with a mysterious "fifth human tribe".

The city sustained serious damage during the dragon war. On numerous occasions it was burned almost to the ground but was rebuilt every time.
The fatal blow was dealt when the June Curse came here. Research proves that it is the original form of astral demons, endowed with extraordinary power.

Most citizens died; the rest were able to escape through portals. The final wave of survivors were saved by a miracle. We may safely say that the Junes elected to split into small groups and spread out across the continent. This allowed them to avoid the Curse for a long time. However, this also led to a gradual cultural regression and assimilation.

Wormfaces later visited the ruins. Perhaps they became sacred locations for former Junes who remember the past."

"You're reading another page from the folder. "Joint report of Nomarkhs Semerkhet, Yasskul Khufukhaf, and Taltal: the Holy Lands research." Here's a fragment:

The conclusions based on the results of our research are fully consistent with our preliminary assessment stated during the historical conference "The June impact on Zem culture."

The following has been proven:

1. There was a large-scale cultural influence expressed in the need to conduct a ritual, during which each of the Zem was required to visit the territories of the former June state and inspect the ruins in order to strengthen motivation in the search for immortality. This fact is confirmed both by the testimonies of witnesses (including the authors of the report) and by the numerous traces of Zem presence on Asee-Teph.

2. Proven fact: a journey of a famous Zem known as Tep took place around 2470 AD (Old Era).

3. The study of the structure known as "Tensess Temple" has provided evidence that the journey made a significant impact on the individual's personality and mind.

4. It has been established that soon after the journey, Tep discovered the nature of Sparks and began a large-scale construction of Spark storage facilities also known as "Tep's Pyramids".

Conclusions:

With a high degree of probability, we conclude that Tep's journey to the ruins of the June civilization helped inspire his scientific breakthrough involving the discovery of Sparks and Immortality. We leave speculations on the nature of knowledge (in particular, the marginal theory that the god of Death appeared before Tep and personally granted him the knowledge) to the readers."

You're reading another page from the folder. "Sarang Petosiris, Tep Cultist's speech". Here's a fragment:

Tep? How dare you say this name?!

Tep is the greatest necromancer of our world! In my past life, I was honored to help him! Tep was studying June magic then.
Junes... Oh yes, they achieved so much. So, Tep studied them. His primary field was blood magic. The Junes knew a thing or two about it. Blood has great power. It has the life power of the Spark. By consuming blood, you consume someone else's power. Why do you think the Great Mages drink dragon blood? Or the Demonologists drink demon blood? Or vampires!

Tep went even further. June magic didn't help them when the Curse appeared... the first demon.

Yes, that's right. The legendary June Curse was a demon. You didn't know? That's weird. I've seen it as clearly as I see you. And you might see it some day! Why? What do you mean - why? It's there somewhere. What did it look like? The last time I saw it, it was following the real Junes. They're extinct now, of course. But there are so many people with June blood in their veins! Why do you think the astral demons look so much like the Curse? It's out there! I can't believe you live in this world and know so little about it.

Tep now consumed Sparks instead of blood. A straightforward way is always faster. But he needed a stock. A stock of Sparks. It wouldn't have worked if Tep hadn't found a record about the Box. Nih's box, of course.

Basically, this world is a trap for Sparks. Nothing can leave it. Tep found the source of the power that's holding it inside without letting anything out. How? I don't know.

Based on this power, he built pyramids. He also created the Plague. You'll have a taste of it when Tep comes back...

Ouch, don't hit me!

The note stops abruptly.

You're tired of reading, but you turn the page. It's "Thibault de Desirae's thoughts on some paradoxes on the Coba Plateau". Here's a fragment:

The story that happened here, on Coba Plateau, still haunts me. When Tep was constructing the pyramids, preparing to destroy his people, this place was the center of his cult.

Contrary to popular belief, the greatest battle between him and the Zem Mechanics took place here, in a place now known as Spectral Gorge. That's where the pyramid with a destroyed top is.

My expedition conducted research and established some facts that contradict the popular interpretation of the story.

First of all, there's the question: who buried Nefer Ur and other mechanics on Hickut (now known as Xadagan), even though they died here, on Coba Plateau?

We also failed to find residual plague in soil and water, even though everything here should still be dead.

Here is an interesting fact learned by my colleague Noel de Blizare from legends of local people now living in the Holy Land.

According to them, death came here. It breathed its black breath, and life itself writhed in agony. Just when there seemed to be no hope, a beautiful girl, a great sorceress, came here. Morning glory flowers grew in her footsteps as she walked. With her power she destroyed death and left no trace. It took her a while to bury all the dead people. She sealed the eternally dying Tep in his main Pyramid known as Asee-Teph.

Who could that be? A Great Mage from the past? An unknown goddess? I'm afraid we'll never know the answers. Maybe Zayan knows something?

I believe these documents prove a lot. But my story of your deeds will not be complete without the description of the final meeting with Nihaz. You found the Sparks of three June heroes, after all.

"Hahaha! You really thought I was hiding the Sparks? Or giving them to someone else? Come on now, it isn't our first game. How could you be so naive?

If I simply wanted to destroy you, why would I waste so much time? Are you really that stupid to think that your actions have no consequences?

I hope you've seen and learned enough. The Junes. The Zem. They've made their choices. Who should they blame but themselves if the choice is wrong? Do you understand now? Perhaps there is still hope for you?

But that's enough. Let's see who wins the bet, shall we?

Ah! You managed to break the rules in a game that only had two rules!

NO help AT ALL! All you did was ask around for help!

Everybody must face the consequences of their foolishness...

Then Klavdia Kalugina intervened, showing up out of the blue.

"Oh, come on. Everyone knows that this bet was null and void from the start. Your tasks are impossible to complete."

"Nevertheless, shehe agreed."

"We don't need to stoop to such trickery! I know you agree with me.

I'm going to pull my rank to declare it void and confiscate everything that was found during the bet.

Especially since none of you have the slightest idea what to do with the Sparks.

Keep on playing your games. Oh, and before you find your tongues... Bye-bye, Daddy and you, hero.

Well, then... I guess we are both left in the dust. My daughter is something else. Come here.

Haha, isn't my daughter clever?

I hope you understand the reason behind all this.

Anyway, I think you've found everything you were looking for. And I'm going to give you a consolation prize, of course.

You can go now. It's time for me to get back to business... In the tavern.

Very interesting story. One centaur huntress received a note from her missing brother. She was very worried about him and asked you to look for him. You had to follow his trail and find the notes he left behind. I can show them to you if you're interested.

... It is an old letter, scribbled on a piece of parchment, or rather, on a piece of rough leather.

Nevertheless, you can recognize the Aoidos language, written by a strong hand not used to writing.

"My dear sister! The wind and the road are calling me. I can't believe this day has come, but I'll be on my way tomorrow. I've always been a strange centaur. Our village is too small for me. I made up my mind. I want to travel, visit places, see the miracles and wonders of the world. Who knows, we might meet again some day. For what it's worth, don't be sad. I'd suffer here if I stayed.

P.S.: Don't worry about me, I'm not careless. I prepared for the long journey!

Here's my checklist:

An extra four of boots;

A bundle of food I picked up in the camp (no idea how long it will keep, though);

An axe. What would I be without it?

My favorite toy centaur (mini me);

A bunch of stuff for the road.

If you wonder where I'll go first, it's the Well of Souls. They say it's the most amazing place on Ammer! I don't know what it is, but that makes it better! Maybe I'll write a song.

Alright, it's taking too long. I'm going to bed, I've got an early morning tomorrow."

"I don't see why people love this Well so much. The morning sun is a thousand times more beautiful, and you can see it from everywhere.

I'm a simple centaur. I'm not even a shaman who talks to spirits. I can't see the whole picture. Come to think of it, why is it even called a "well"? It's no good for collecting water. Oh heavens, it is a weird place, indeed.

While I was grabbing a bite, I overheard a conversation. They were talking about Demon Hunters whose camp they liberated from demons a while ago. They're so brave! They fly through astral and hunt astral monsters there. They've been everywhere. I decided I should pay them a visit and listen to their stories. I hear nature is very beautiful there.

My hooves are aching, but adventure is calling! No time for rest!"

"I was too arrogant to ignore my aches... I hit my head on a branch and twisted two ankles! Thank the spirits it happened near the camp. The locals helped me and gave me food and water. They also told me a lot of stories. It almost feels like home.

I didn't leave home just to settle down somewhere else, even in a nice place like this. I looked at the sky and felt that my heart was full. The open road is calling my name again. Where should I head? I remembered the story of Kyros and Aellona. Kyros, the poor fellow, defeated our chief and earned the tribe's respect... After Aellona died, he went mad and messed up everything. Such a sad story, but also beautiful. I could write a song about it.

I decided to visit Aellona's grave. I'll leave in the morning."

"Oh spirits, I have the strangest feeling. It's like guilt for being alive when Aellona is dead. Enough of being sad, though. I should leave a note in a safe place, away from prying eyes...

I'm asking myself why I'm doing this. Do I want to leave a trail? Do I secretly hope that someone might follow my tracks? Do I expect someone to find me? My sister, a secret admirer, or just someone simply wandering around the world?

Since I started making notes, I should continue. Now I'm wondering where it will take me!

It cheered me up. Where will I go next? I think I'll visit Polis. It isn't far from here. I heard it was a lovely place full of people. Maybe I can find a friend there."

"I didn't expect Polis to be such an amazing place. Aoidos managed to build so many things here. What a gifted nation! Just like us.

I came across a weird vagabond who was looking for something, mumbling nonsense. I tried to run away, but he just wouldn't leave me alone! One thing led to another, and here we are, relaxing after exploring this city's every nook and cranny. To understand how much fun we had, just imagine how hard it is for a CENTAUR to climb onto a roof. I'm not sure I can repeat that!

My friend loves secrecy and conspiracies! Poor fellow, he just can't see past these mysteries. I should remember to leave him a note about my future plans. It should make him happy."

"I'm sorry to leave you, my friend, but the road's a-callin'.

Besides, even if I stay, can a centaur find a job in Polis? This is how it is...

You've helped me realize something. If you keep searching, you'll eventually find something. I didn't know that at first, but then I understood. You just have a goal and strive to reach it. It doesn't matter what other people think. It requires strong will. Above all, don't lose yourself trying to solve another mystery!

Perhaps our paths will cross later. If you're interested, I'm heading to the South of Dion Mountain Range, beyond the Pearl Slopes, to see those demons people keep talking about."

"Demons are truly amazing creatures. I didn't expect them to look like that. And they communicate with the help of images they conjure up in your mind. Marvelous! It's strange that many consider them evil and dark creatures. Of course, they can be frightening. And they don't really understand humor. But they are so beautiful!

People despise rats as well, but have rats ever hurt anyone? They're living beings who want their share of food and water! Hardly any rat ever crawled inside a house with malicious intent!

Some demons never heard of centaurs, so I left a note to the most curious of them. He gave me something in return...

This is a lovely place. I'll sleep here, and then I'll head to Triquetrum. The Aoidos mentioned some kind of "energies" there. I need to see them."

"I think I know what Aoidos meant by "energies". We'd say this place was blessed by the spirits. They might have over-blessed it a bit. Everything here seems ordinary and miraculous at the same time.

The most interesting places are never talked about. You only get to learn about them by chance: overhear a conversation or see a turn in the road... I'm getting more and more confident that I made the right decision. You can't just sit around peacefully when there's a big world outside with so much to see!

I hope some other strange adventurer who finds my notes and follows my tracks will never regret their decision!

I discovered that I left my favorite toy behind. It's not that important, but it holds so many good memories. I'll drop by our camp tonight. Just need to make sure not to run into my sister or friends."

Just think about it. No two-legged creature can imagine how hard it is to sneak quietly on four muscular legs.

I got carried away and walked through the whole the camp! I can't brag about it to anyone, but it's something I can write down in my notes!

Familiar places look different at night. You get to notice things you never noticed before. It makes you understand things you couldn't until now. But enough of "philosophizing", as Aoidos used to say.

My sister was asleep as I grabbed the toy. I think she sensed my presence but never woke up. I don't know how. She might have sighed in a special way. I grew up with her, so I can feel her with my heart.

I know she will forgive me. She won't think I ran away.

There's only one place left to visit. It's the Site of Power. They say that the swords are always clashing there. I'll go to the champions' camp and get drunk to leave these lands without a second thought."

"All right, the swords here aren't always clashing. I didn't see a single battle while I was here. I guess I was incredibly lucky.

Boy, did we get drunk! I had no idea so many people can ride my back all at once! An idea of giving people rides never occurred to me in the first place.

I received a mug with my name on it - somebody carved it with a knife. I was called "a great man and an average horse". They also invited me to stop by whenever I'm around. I will stop by on my way back, perhaps.

They say alcohol won't solve your problems. It sure won't, but a good party can chase away the gloom. It's important to maintain the balance... It's very important.

I'm going to the Dionic Archipelago. I've heard a lot of wonderful things about it. I'll see you on the docks, my imaginable follower."

"The docks don't seem extraordinary after you've seen Polis. Just barrels and crates... The flight was something to remember, though. I've never... flown? or sailed? Never traveled much. Anyway, seeing it is worth a thousand words.

I found a way to entertain myself, though. I assumed an air of importance and started walking around, opening boxes and barrels, examining their contents. People regarded me with suspicion, but no one dared to approach me. I looked very confident and somewhat menacing. I took nothing, though. I was just curious. Only one thing looked interesting: a sphere made of a semi-transparent gemstone, with fine dust whirling and glowing inside...

It's getting dark. The dockers told me there was a village not too far away. I'll spend the night and hit the road in the morning."

"It turns out I'm fond of villages, no matter who lives there (unless it's someone who wants to rip out your guts). They all look alike in a way. Whatever happens in the world, they live their own lives, look after their households, be it centaurs or humans...

I'm getting more and more romantic. I wonder if the travels awoke that in me, or if it's something all adventurers suffer from. I neither can nor want to figure it out! I think I'll just go with the flow.

I've been dreaming about lying alone in a pasture, far away from home, without knowing what lies ahead, simply admiring the stars. It's time to make the dream come true. Let me find the nearest pasture and head there."

"So I've been watching the sunset. I'm writing this note while the sun is still up, so I wouldn't ruin a starry night by scribbling things down.

Whenever the stars are visible, I don't feel like writing. They make you feel so small and unimportant... You start thinking about what's happening up there, the amazing and significant events.

I'm feeling nostalgic. I suddenly remembered my sis and my dear village. How are they doing back home? I'm not homesick, not really. But it'd be nice to know that they are doing fine.

Back to real life tomorrow. I'm taking part in all kinds of local entertainment - as a spectator first. I'm going to Coliseum in the morning. In the meantime..."

"It's so much fun! Pegasus flights, ball throwing, the crowd cheering... The applause, I was told, is when all people start clapping their hands. I tried that with my hooves. I think it made me deaf in my right ear!

It doesn't matter what they tell me - I must try it myself. I can't wait, my hooves are shaking. I'm going to do it. No matter what. Everyone should! My next stop is Pegasus's back. End of story."

My request to participate made the jaws drop. They tried to talk me out of it, but their leader decided that a Centaur riding a Pegasus would be great publicity. He gave me the most powerful stallion!

Now picture their faces when I took out a piece of parchment and started scribbling - right there, in the air, on the Pegasus's back! As if I were an incredible poet of ancient times! That's what I'm doing right now. The parchment crackles and leaps out of my hands. There's too much magic here! I don't know if I can hold it. Gotta go somewhere quiet after the flight. Like the local maze where you can easily get lost..."

"I can't quite figure out where I am. All turns look the same. Here's a gazebo, and there's another one. I sat down to collect my thoughts while I'm writing another note.

After my spectacular ride, they allowed me to take part in other activities. I'm a local star - or, maybe, a local crazy. Go figure!

This place is... Creepy. Not only paths, but thoughts get twisted here. Someone evil created this place. Someone who enjoys watching people wander helplessly. Why on earth did I come here? And these Minotaurs... are staring. Some would say we're alike, but it's hard to imagine two more different species if you ask me. Don't even argue with that!

I must choose something simpler next time. An obstacle course, for example. The whole point is to get to the finish line first. Unsophisticated but still fun!

Now I should find a way out. If all else fails, they should remember about me and get me out of here... I hope."

"Yay, I was the best! ...in kicking down the obstacles. No surprise. It's made for the two-legged.

 I rushed towards the end, kicking down every obstacle in my way. I was so angry! Tried to be careful, of course - I didn't want to hurt anyone.

It's a good thing I was running behind everyone else. They were waiting for me at the finish line to let me cross it first as a sign of respect. No way, I thought. So I pushed the well-mannered Aoidoi beyond the finish line by force! They deserved this victory, so let them take it!

I'll balance the loss at the race. That's where I'll finish first!"

I wasn't first, of course. But the fourth place is an excellent result for a novice.

I even contemplated becoming a regular participant. It gives you a truly unique sensation: wind in the face and speed, just like on a hunt, but you run faster and don't have to kill anyone. However, it's nonsense. I know I'll get bored soon. But it's worth trying.

I've got this idea of a race where everyone bumps into one another until the strongest and the most skillful remains. I wonder if anything like this exists in the world?

Observatory is my destination now. I heard a lot about it while studying the local landmarks. They say it has a lot of smart guys who will surely advise me what else I should visit."

"Oh spirits, I don't know what to say! Some places and events just change your very being in an instant! The Observatory took my breath away.

I learned a lot. They told me about other worlds, about Architects and time travel, about the endless Astral. News like this take time to digest.

It will take even longer to see it all!

Whoever is reading this note, I'll say goodbye. I don't know where I'm going, but it's somewhere far away. I'm looking for... I don't know what, but I must find it.

Go your own way. I'm sure it will be legendary. If you want it, of course.

I left a gift for my reader. Find the small crate. It contains the most valuable thing.

Take it with you. In a way, I'm grateful. It was a journey that we took together.

Good luck, whoever you are."

It's stored in Cosmos's Observatory, but I copied the information from it for the Historians' archives.

"Precious crumbs of knowledge about other worlds, collected by the hero of our world, Sarnaut."
Gray Prince! A truly mysterious personality which many believed did not exist at all. But you managed to collect important information about them.

"My dear Nezeb, why did you reject our plan? Why did you agree to this insane duel?

We had been preparing for so long... Placed our people in certain positions, hid caches with weapons... We were ready to set out and dethrone the emperor of Valir!

And you ruined everything... Now I stand among the endless sands with no idea how to find you. My people can search every street in the bustling cities of the north. But here in the south, in the barren and deadly desert, I am powerless."

"You have changed so much over the years, my friend... Really, I did not expect to hear from you again. Time spares no one!

If only you knew what I had to do to get my hands on that thing that would extend my life... The Conclave jealously guards its secrets, and Tensess no longer trusts me.

The sacrifices I made to get a little drop of dragon blood? I won't talk about it. I'm glad to know that you were able to find one of the hearts here, in the deserts of the south. Although it's upsetting that you remembered me so late!

But our alliance still stands. Kania awaits it hero."

"I was happy to see your new land. It's so different from the northern countries!

Kania lost the core that allowed it to survive the wars with the Orcs. The former unity is only a memory now: the land is torn apart by disputes and squabbles. The Valir grandchildren are ready to rip out each other's throats for a shred of power. Tensess is too soft to keep them in line.

People are tired of constant squabbles. They remember the hero of the war. You!

It's time to come back and claim what is rightfully yours!"

"Kania ceded its territories to Nezeb, and this gave rise to a new Empire - the Xadagan Empire. Of course, there is still much to be done. The conquest is not over yet. Soon the whole world will submit to our rule.

For now... I'll retreat into the shadows. With a supply of dragon blood, I will exist for centuries, guarding the treasures of our Emperor. The desert offers ideal conditions for hiding what needs to be hidden. Artifacts that grant power over jinns. Treasures that can buy anyone. Knowledge that must be unattainable for the time being...

I will find those who will help me and Nezeb without realizing it. Those who consider him their enemy but serve his interests. Everyone who is unhappy with the current situation in the Empire. It will be the brotherhood of the last shelter."
Nezeb! The great conqueror and founder of Xadagan, he is still highly revered in the Empire. Few people can say they knew him closely... But you managed to learn part of his story.

"The desert... the place of my exile...

Betrayed by my sworn brother, dismissed by my teacher, forgotten by my people...

I am no one, and my name was struck from the pages of history that I helped make...

The cursed duel... I could have won it! One thing failed me - my resolve. I was not ready to fight someone I considered a brother! We went through all the hardships together. It made me falter, but not him! He was ready to crush his brother in the name of his ideals. Well, now I understand what I should have done... I only need to cross this...

Desert... the place of my exile..."

"What did we know about this place? Our homeland is the land of green forests and fields. Here the golden dunes stretch to the horizon... And it feels like there is no life here.

But this impression is misleading... My arrival was noticed by more than one pair of eyes. Like rocks falling from the heavens, I drew a line of fire across the sky. I saw those who stared at this "omen" with awe and horror.

Who are they? My teacher spoke of other tribes... The powerful Junes, creators of the empire that ruled this continent? The hard-working Zem who built their pyramids along the River Aether? The proud Knos that crossed the oceans on their ships?

But they all went away. Their time ran out.

Finally, my people - the Aro tribes who are now ready to take their place in the sun... There's nothing for them here! There's the fifth tribe... Ugra."

"The locals! A pale imitation of humans. Dirty, superstitious nomads! "Descendants of the god of Ugra", "chosen" and "undefeated"! Hah!

But they gave me shelter. Their legends vaguely say that a man "who fell from the heavens" will appear in the desert. He will lead their people to world domination. It's laughable. They are just a handful of tribes living in a forsaken desert. That's the only reason they were allowed to exist. What do they know about the world? About the countless cities of Kania? About indestructible elven fortresses? About the Orcs' Horde which was one step away from conquering this continent?

World domination? Truly, this illusion must be the only gratifying thing the exiles have in this desert!"

"The poverty and wretchedness of local existence is embellished with fairy tales that old people love to tell so much. In the evenings, everyone gathers around campfires to listen to another tale...

Fantasies! Nothing more. Despite having so little, this nation dreams of so much!

They speak of magic! Of dormant jinn kingdoms under the sands that long to awaken. Of treasures in secret caves. Of power that will be bestowed upon whoever finds the passage hidden deep in the mountains.

After laughing about it openly, I agreed to travel to the mountains. Of course we won't find anything there..."

"Where there were only oases in the desert, the walls of cities now rise. The howl of jackals was replaced by the noise of countless caravans.

They are no longer the people of Ugra! They are the Xada people now, the Xadaganians. They don't need to be descendants of a god if they already have a god, and that god is me!

I slayed all the tribal leaders in a sword fight, although I must admit they did not stand a chance against my new powers. But I see beyond all that...

I see a new Empire, cleansed of the mistakes of the past, devoid of the flaws that were so intolerant to me in Kania. My new Empire will be flawless like a sharpened edge. People inhabiting it will not be of flesh and blood, but of stone and steel Having unflinching fortitude, they will be capable of incredible things..."

"The final preparations are complete. The desert is completely in my power, and my forces have approached the borders of my former homeland.

Perhaps Tensess and the others recognize the magnitude of what they are up against. I think they suspect that I managed to entice part of the Conclave over to my side. Many are unhappy with the state of affairs in Kania, the constant disputes between the heirs of Valir. I will bring a much needed order.

My students will come to Kania with me. I spent many centuries to find and train the Xadaganians that have the gift of magic. Alas, my subjects have nonexistent magical talents, which they make up for with diligence and obedience.

And of course, I will have the jinn people on my side. My secret weapon! I spent many years searching for their shelters, developing subjugation spells, binding them to lamps and rings...

Finally, my last and most secret tool. The Gray Prince and his numerous spies who are ready to open the gates of the cities for my armies...

In a few years, the entire Kania will be part of my Empire!"
Be friends, you say? Okay then.
Aaah! Gorluxor is alive! Alive! He will be here soon! He is going to kill Soliskar, who is supporting the allods from being swallowed by the Astral and rules the draconids... Oh, it hurts!

You have to fight three of my disciples and defeat each of them. But that alone will not be enough. By besting each of my disciples you will only prove that speaking to you now is not a total waste of my time. But if you show me a real fighter's spirit and swagger, perhaps I might deign to actually continue this conversation.

At first, when you spoke about a meeting with the Servant of Tensess, I admit I did not believe it. But why would you want to deceive me? So I decided to rouse the enemy, compel them to make mistakes and reveal themselves. The plan worked perfectly.
When I gave the order to speed up construction by revving up the generators to maximum power, that's when that sanctimonious fool had to personally intervene to prevent us from completing the construction. So I caught him red-handed and gave him a glorious thrashing! Sparks everywhere! But his strength seemed inexhaustible, and in your world, alas, I am burdened by certain limitations. So, to be frank, that exploding generator did right by both of us when it interrupted your flight.
Now our enemy is defeated and fled in fear. Moreover, he lost a fair amount of his power, which was absorbed into the Cradle, strengthening it.
And I strongly advise that you forget about the meeting with the Servant of Tensess, the duel and everything else. No one can know about it. Believe me, if you wind up in the Purgatory again, he will pretend that he doesn't know you at all. You are but a grain of sand to him, your life - a moment in time before eyes of eternity. What happened is not your problem, not at all. It isn't even your world's problem, my friend. Your problem is Sarn, and that's what you ought to focus on if you wish to survive. And forget about today's duel.

The luckiest guilds will be able to take control over an allod in all its phases. It won't be easy, though.

It all started with demons...

Demons… No one really knows where they came from… It is only known that they have been present in our world for a long time. The famous Great Mage Skrakan encountered the first demon, and it took him great effort to defeat it.

The second time they invaded all allods at once, and this event is now known as the Night of Astral Portals... Millions died...

Then their invasions started happening all the time. No one knew how to deal with them...

Demonology is a school of magic just like any elemental one. Or witchcraft. Or mysticism. Or necromancy... It doesn't matter - people still look at us like we're lepers, and the Church has imposed penance on us.

But remember this: we are not some crazy cultists. Demons are not our allies or an object of worship. They are no better than guinea pigs. Demons are our window to the world of new magical heights, nothing more.

It was a miracle that we managed to persuade Aidenus to let us open an office in the capital.

Now it is headed by Vranomir Temnov, my brother. If you can get off this island and get to Novograd, find him. He will explain what to do next.

Well, my advice is simple: do not neglect your gift. Use it. We can take many forms - choose one you like and follow your path.

May the Light bless you!

Initially, there was no resurrection in our world. Creatures died, and it was either necromancers who could bring them back in the form of undead, or some complex and dangerous rituals of the Great Mages.

In the year 911 of the Allods Era, an event occurred in Sarnaut that forever changed the usual routine of life - resurrection became possible in case of premature death.

As it turned out in the end, it was a gift from Tensess, the Great Mage of the League, who died in battle during the capture of the capital of Kania. Tensess made this gift not only to the League, but also to the Empire, believing that old enemies should unite in the face of a new external threat.

It happened like this: when the Spark of the Great Tensess, who died during the invasion of demons, ended up in Tep's Pyramid, his strength was enough to repel the ancient evil. The sinister necromancer was banished, and his cursed Pyramid became a temple. Tensess Temple!As it turned out in the end, it was a gift from Tensess, the Great Mage of the League who died in battle during the capture of the capital of Kania. However, after the death of the great Nezeb, our leader and teacher, and of his mentor Skrakan, the power grew - the Light became even more powerful. Nezeb and Skrakan died defending the world against demons, and their sacrifice meant as much as that of Tensess.

His Spark ended up in Tep's Pyramid, and it was powerful enough to repel the ancient evil. The sinister necromancer was banished, and his cursed Pyramid became a temple. Tensess Temple!

At the beginning, no one knew about the resurrection. But then an astral ship crashed near the Holy Land. After a heroic death, the sailors found themselves on an unknown allod. "Is this hell, paradise, or non-existence?" they must have asked. Later, they discovered the Tensess Temple. After meeting a smuggler innkeeper, they were able to return to their homeland where they told everyone what happened to them. Cases of resurrection began to multiply.

Those who were able to resurrect said they visited Purgatory and saw a giant fire-headed angel who became known as the Servant of Tensess. It turned out that he releases people from Purgatory only after a certain time which is determined by the sins of the deceased.

But there was also a way to get out ahead of schedule - by donating drops of precious Mirra.

Yes. Unfortunately, not everyone is resurrected...

Firstly, those whose lifespan has come to an end, in old age. Their Sparks go somewhere else...

Secondly, those who reject the Gift of Tensess itself, reject the commandments of the Church, and pose a threat to the whole world cannot be resurrected - like the numerous cultists, demon worshipers, and heretics. But there is an exception - ignorant pagans who do not know about the Gift can be resurrected through the rituals of the priests of the Church. Because if they don't know what they're missing, they can't reject it.

Thirdly, those whose bodies have been irreversibly damaged cannot be resurrected. For example, they dissolved in the astral or were destroyed. The thing is, the Spark needs something to return to. Those who, for example, have their heads cut off cannot be resurrected - such injuries are too severe to be healed.

These brave priestesses are responsible for ensuring that the bodies of the dead are not lost while their Sparks remain in Purgatory.

Each priestess has her own territory which she oversees or asks others to oversee. As soon as she detects a deceased, she transfers them to a special altar where the body will safely await resurrection.

Also, these priestesses heal light and medium wounds using Light magic. In the League they serve in the Order of Mercy, and in the Empire, the Order of Compassion. Of course, although they work selflessly for the benefit of all living, their labors require payment - so they are always ready to sell the holy Mirra needed for donations to the Servant of Tensess.

Wishing to make astral travel safer, these priestesses also enchant cabins on ships. As soon as someone dies in the astral plane, a special spell transfers the deceased to the ship's infirmary where resurrection will take place shortly after. At the request of the Free Traders, similar places are also being set up in various arenas and stadiums.

And if the ship is completely destroyed, the spell can transfer the team to the capital. Of course, maintaining such magic is expensive, but it is paid from the treasury of the state.

Light Magic is another commodity granted by Tensess. What makes it different from other magic is the fact that it's available to anyone. The main thing is faith. If you believe in the Light, this magic becomes available to you. And if earlier magic was something few people had access to, now anyone can acquire abilities regardless of their status or knowledge. This changed the balance of power in the world and continues to change it to this day. The Magic of Light is a great power.

Its abilities are diverse - it can both resurrect and heal. But most importantly, it can fight against the enemies of the Light, smiting them.

Very quickly, two directions formed among the inhabitants of Sarnaut: the Priests who were more focused on healing. And the Templars who considered it their duty to protect others.

You understand, all these events with the gods left their mark. Many witnessed what was happening in our world, many saw the battle of the mad Kyros and Servant of Tensess! Demons, Architects, the appearance of the Aoidoi - all this needed explanation.

After long negotiations, the Church of Light and the Trinity Church decided to unite. As for dogmas, we have yet to establish them. It's clear that there is something outside of our world that we have no idea about. However, it is clear that the Light is one for everyone - for the League, the Empire, the Pridens, and even the Tekyan. To find the Source of this Light - that's the purpose of the new Church! The Church of the Eternal Light...

It will be led by a collegial body - the Synod of Hierarchs. It will include representatives of each of the races who believe in the Light.

The Church of the League, also known as the Church of Light, was founded first. Its tenets are based on the fact that the Gift of Tensess and the magic of Light became available to the inhabitants of Sarnaut thanks to the sacrifice of Tensess who died fighting the demons. Tensess's Spark went to Tep's Pyramid and defeated this necromancer, expelling him from the Pyramid.

Using the power of the Pyramid, Tensess granted resurrection to all the inhabitants of Sarnaut.

However, was Tensess's sacrifice something unique? Or perhaps Nezeb and Skrakan, who sacrificed themselves in the battle against demons, are no different from Tensess? Could the Great Nezeb forget about his followers even in death?

Our Trinity Church teaches sensibly: Tensess's sacrifice is equal to the sacrifice of Nezeb and Skarkan. All of them are great martyrs of the great war.

The Church of the League refused to accept Nezeb as a saint, even though they recognize the sainthood of the five Imperial Great Mages who died when the world split into allods. The thing is, corrupt hierarchs are afraid... afraid of the truth, because everyone understands that the Empire is superior to the League in everything!

In addition, our Church is based on equality: we do not have Superiors; we have commissars and political leaders who are equal in rights, and the same goes for church ministers of other nations of the Empire. Each of these political leaders can head the respective committee after a closed and secret ballot. In the rotten League everything is controlled through nepotism and bribery.

Now Elizaveta Rysina, the head of the City Council, has taken over the helm of the Church Affairs Committee.

The Church of the League, also known as the Church of Light, was founded first. Its tenets are based on the fact that the Gift of Tensess and the magic of Light became available to the inhabitants of Sarnaut thanks to the sacrifice of Tensess who died fighting the demons. Tensess's Spark went to Tep's Pyramid and defeated this necromancer, expelling him from the Pyramid.

Using the power of the Pyramid, Tensess granted resurrection to all the inhabitants of Sarnaut.

The Empire did not accept this Gift at first. Even in the time of Nezeb, attempts were made to use the new magic, but it soon became clear that without faith in the sacrifice of Tensess, the Light magic was inaccessible. Nezeb did not instill the new religion in the Empire, not wanting to deify his eternal enemy.

Everything changed after the Great Astral Campaign. In this battle, the soldiers of the Empire fought side by side with the Kanians, and the servants of the Church of Light treated their wounds. Wanting to use the magic of Light, the Xadaganian Committee decided to create their own "Church" where they began to revere Tensess along with Nezeb and Skrakan who died during the Great Astral Campaign.

According to the teachings of this "Trinity Church", the sacrifices of Tensess, Nezeb, and Skrakan were considered equal, and they were all declared great martyrs of the great war. This is how the Empire got its own Church and its own priests using the magic of Light.

Of course, we all understand that it is only thanks to Tensess that this Gift exists. The Empire also understands this. For several years now it has been fighting for the Holy Land where his Temple is located.

Our Church is governed by the Council of Priests which consists of the priests of all allods. The same Council chooses its leader. It's now Voisvet Belov, the templar of the first circle and the governor of the Kanian Archipelago.

Soon after the Cataclysm, the Great Mages noticed a strange phenomenon, clearly of a magical nature. The time of its emergence indicated that it was somehow connected to the Astral.

The Astral was magically affecting the inhabitants of Sarnaut. The twelve tides of that force were detected. Each had different properties and impacted the people in its own way. Without any doubt, the phenomenon was a result of the Cataclysm.

For a long time, there was no unity among the Great Mages on the issue of the nature of this phenomenon. Many of them conducted experiments in an effort to confirm their theory. All these theoretical studies had practical results. It soon became clear that a resident of Sarnaut could undergo initiation by becoming the "carrier" of one specific tide. This magical symbiosis grants the initiate special abilities and powers. It was quite easy to distinguish one adept from another: those affected by the wave acquired a distinctive magical glowing halo.

For a long time, the secret of the "astral tides" remained unsolved, and only in the tenth century of the New Era, the truth was revealed.

During the Cataclysm, many Great Mages died, and the mechanism for containing the Astral was not developed for some time. It took the lives of twelve members of the Conclave to curb the Astral. But when humans or elves become Great Mages, they gain immortality! It was immortality that allowed the Spark of Tensess to survive in the Astral and gave it the strength to take control of Tep's Pyramid. And knowing this, how can one consider it a coincidence that after the Cataclysm exactly twelve astral tides appeared - which is the number of dead Great Mages who had developed the Astral Containment Ritual!

Skrakan and Zayan remembered their names. The names of those who, like Tensess himself, served the world even after their death. Their sacrifice was not in vain. Their power is constantly present in the world, giving the Great Mages the ability to hold allods and granting the people of Sarnaut a part of their strength. In the year 921 of the New Age, the names of the Twelve Martyrs were declared, and each force tide was given a name. Anyone could pass the ritual of initiation and become an adept of one of the forces. That's how the mystical Institute of the Twelve Martyrs was established.

The people of Sarnaut believe in their Patrons - the Twelve Great Martyrs who gave their lives in the name of saving the world and bestowed their blessing upon every living creature. Each inhabitant of the allods goes through the Initiation Ritual when they reach a certain age, becoming an adept of one of the magical forces.

You, too, have undergone this ritual!

No one knows for sure. The necromancer Tep, who doomed his people, had conducted a thorough research into the nature of Sparks.

While studying the nature of death, Tep realized that every creature had a certain essence, a spark of life which was enclosed in the body and left it with death. Many called this Spark a "soul" or "divine essence", but Tep tried to approach this issue more practically. He learned to catch other people's Sparks to use their power and gain immortality.

Sages say a lot about Sparks - that they are a part of every soul, that it's a gift that grants free will. It is also believed that Sparks cannot be destroyed. That even when extinguished, they leave a tiny particle that can be reignited and filled with power. That their power comes from the very essence of the world, forming a single whole with its soul.

"Sparks are incomprehensible because they cannot be comprehended, indestructible because they cannot be destroyed," Tensess himself once said.

Perhaps you are interested in something else... Are there creatures without Sparks? Yes, those are the undead, all kinds of zombies and ghouls, just dead bodies filled with the power of a necromancer who raises them. They only have the memory of their body. It's a different person in every other regard. But there are cases when the Spark returns to its dead body - that's how it happened with the Zem people.

Ghosts, on the other hand, are a completely different phenomenon... Some ghosts are just an echo, a replica of the events of the past revived thanks to magic. Such ghosts also don't have Sparks, although they are often filled with the energy of their reflection. But there are rebellious souls, the ether body and the Spark linked together - they cannot leave our world and are forced to exist in this form.

We will take what we need. We will capture the valley - and the power of the Ambrosia will be our weapon against Nihaz.

Listen to me carefully, fighter!

In the center of the valley is the largest deposit of the Ambrosia. It is guarded by this giant log, Cypress. It hates us.

Now it's weak. Our mission is to bring it down. If the Cypress falls, we will win and take control of the valley.

The natives will try to stop us and heal the Treant. If they succeed, we will have to retreat and leave the valley.

Cypress has strong bark. Our A-22 Invaders can penetrate it, but they need powerful fuel from the local Sources.

Listen up!

These are rare and powerful sorceresses of Eden. They are trying to heal Cypress and ruin our plans.

I order you to take them out first.

Healers also consume Seeds of Power to become stronger or respawn. Keep the enemy from capturing the Sources and eliminate those who carry the Seeds.

That way we won't let the enemy win.

They are our key to victory. Only their fire can burn through Cypress's strong bark.

But there is a drawback: these machines target only the Treant. They need your protection. Keep the local savages away from them.

If they break an Invader, only a new Seed of Power can repair it.

While the Invader is alive, use the Seeds to increase its combat power and destroy the Cypress even faster.

This will give us an advantage over the Healers.

It's too early for you to fight, soldier! First deal with Comrade Catherina's tasks and decide which side you are on.

But I respect curiosity. Need a briefing?

There are four Sources of power in the valley. If we capture them, we can get fuel for the Invaders.

But the enemy is vigilant. If the Children control the Source, you will have to chop all the Source Protectors for firewood first, otherwise you won't be able to access its power.

Then enter the Source and concentrate. If no one interrupts you, the Source will obey and start producing Seeds of Power for us.

A Seed of Power is a powerful concentrate of local energy. Without this power, we won't be able to bring down Cypress.

Captured Sources produce Seeds. They are small at first, but they ripen over a couple of minutes.

The ripe seed must be taken from the Source and quickly delivered to the center of the valley, so we can install and fuel our A-22 Invaders.

The respect of the entire Sarnaut!

And generous rewards in Dendrite Coins. Our guys will restock your ammunition for them, and they might even procure some rare equipment.

The better you perform in battle, the more you get.

Fight for the Sources, destroy the enemies, deliver the Seeds to our Invaders, and eliminate the Healers. Every action counts. I personally oversee everything.

All clear?

Go!
The Great Tree gave us life. Now it's our turn to protect it.

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

t:
Look - all the rivers of the Ambrosia flow to the center of the valley. The mighty Cypress guards the Ambrosia there.

Now it's weak. Several times a day, the enemy attacks him, trying to break him. If Cypress falls, the Expedition will win and take control of the valley.

If we manage to fully heal Cypress, he will put the enemy to flight, and the valley will remain ours.

Our great Healers can heal the Cypress, but they need nourishment from the Seeds of Power. You can get them from the Sources along the edges of the valley.

But first things first.

Only the great daughters of Eden can heal the wounds of Cypress.

But they have to focus entirely on healing, so they can't defend themselves. Protect them from the enemy.

If a Healer falls, only a new Seed can bring her back to life.

If you offer the Seed to a living Healer, her strength will increase for a while, and Cypress's wounds will heal even faster.

This is how we will help Cypress survive against the Invaders.

These iron monsters, created by the children of Sarn, are able to burn through Cypress's bark with their fire.

The expedition captures the Sources and uses the energy of the Seeds of Power to create and strengthen these monsters.

Destroy the Invaders as soon as they appear, and do not allow the enemy to use the Sources and Seeds of Power for their own purposes!

You are eager to go into battle, but can we trust you, Child of Sarn? First learn the lessons of the All-Mother and decide which side you are on.

But if you want, I'll tell you about our war. Perhaps this will influence your choice.

Are you listening carefully?

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

t:
The valley is nourished by four Sources of power, and by nature they are free. But we can turn the power of the Source to our advantage.

First, if the source is already captured by the Expedition, you will have to defeat all the Source Protectors first, otherwise you won't be able to access its power.

Then enter the Source and concentrate. If no one interrupts your concentration, the Source will begin to produce Seeds of Power for us.

The seed of power is a powerful concentration of the energy of life itself. Without them, we can't protect Cypress.

Seeds are born in the Sources and belong to those who own the Source. They are small at first but ripen quickly.

Take the ripe seed from the source and deliver it to the heart of the valley as quickly as possible to revive our great Healers or strengthen those who are fighting for the life of the Cypress.

A reward? We are protecting our home!

I know. Eden is not your home, Child of Sarn. You stand against your people to help us.

Fight for us, and I will generously bestow on you the Tears of the All-Mother You can pay our craftsmen with them for the supplies you need.

 The better you perform in battle, the greater reward I can promise you.

Fight for the Sources, eliminate the enemies, deliver the Seeds to our Healers, and destroy the Invaders. All-Mother sees everything. Each feat will be counted.

Are you surprised that we also have boys and girls? Such was the will of the All-Mother which made us look like creatures that live on an infinite number of worlds, and which are like you. But the resemblance is only superficial.

We distribute pollen, which then falls on the flowers of the Great Tree, and then fruits form on them. When the time comes, this fruit falls to the ground, and a new Child emerges from it, ready for life in this world and able to speak and walk. I know things are a little different for you, and this is very curious.  Maybe you can tell me about it someday?

My task is to ensure that nothing happens to fallen fruits. Although they are well protected by their dense skin, anything can happen, and it would be a tragedy to lose a new member of the tribe. After all, they might be the one destined to become the germ of a new Great Tree!

Look at me. At any of us. You see the fruit on our heads? This fruit is the focus of our life force. The fruit is the germ of a future Great Tree. This is the true purpose of our existence - to keep the cycle going.

Sooner or later our Tree will die. But new shoots will sprout from its remains, spawned by one of us. Isn't this a true miracle?

I am one of the hunters of our tribe.  I think you are wondering - "why does the tribe have hunters if they feed on Ambrosia."  But our task is a little different from foraging, although personally I have nothing against predators who kill to survive, because this is all part of the Great Cycle. And our animals are also full of Ambrosia, and if there is no other way, then we feed on them.

First of all, by virtue of our nature, we must maintain the balance. Sometimes, unreasonable beasts behave... unreasonably. In some places predators oppress herbivores, in others herbivores have become too prolific and have trampled down all the grass. It is important to maintain the balance.

This is especially true for large creatures like Treebors - ordinary predators won't be able to defeat those.

The important thing is that no life will be taken in vain, because their bodies will become humus, an important ingredient in soil. We start hunting only after performing all necessary rituals, with an understanding of our goal and the blessing of the All-Mother.
Greetings! Remember, the forest can be dangerous...
Well? I'm losing my mind here.
So it was you who took down Waterlily and Reed? If It had been me...
Creatures like you keep trying to kill us. I will fight to protect the Children of the All-Mother!
You wear a hard shell, but your bark underneath is quite soft.  We are stronger than you on the inside.

I'm so happy you found him!

I worry about my future brethren like I worry about myself. Every seed of the Great Tree is precious to Eden.

It's too bad you couldn't find him...

If someone has abducted our brother, I swear I will find the thief and send him to the beginning of the cycle with my own hands.

I'll do that!

Good luck, , and be careful.

Quiet! They'll spot us...

Look what I found! So heavy! I barely managed to bring it here!
Ugh... alright! I'll help you at least. But you owe me now - don't you forget that.

What do you mean, why?

We must study every creature and every plant in this world! Our survival and the success of the entire Expedition depend on it! This won't do any harm to the tree - there is still a bunch of these nuts under it.
Why would I? I had to risk my neck to get it!

Oh, that's...

That's amazing! I hope I'll be allowed to study them... We must immediately report to the base! I can't wait for show Elena my discovery!

Please don't take it away!

Oh yeah?

You know, ... You are a hero. You do important work. And you're on friendly terms with Catherina and Felix.

And me? Just a small research assistant, one of the many cogs in this big machine. You don't even know my name.

I don’t know why you need this nut, but this is my chance to become a bigger cog, which will make me a little happier. Just imagine if they let me do real research! The Expedition would benefit greatly from it. And so would the world...

What do you say, ?

You will be attacking it.

Give me a sign, and I'll poke it with my thorn. Its skin is thick, but the sap on the tip of my thorn will keep making it angrier.

Rage will make its strength fill its veins. Each drop of its sap that falls on the ground is priceless - collect them.

But even in rage, there should be balance, otherwise the sap of the beast will be filled not with strength, but with madness. Don't let the rage of the Treebor dissipate, but don't let it go berserk either.

We need to survive the fight. The Treebor is merciless - if you fall, it will trample you.

Mint can protect you. If you fall, give her a sign, and the forest charms will protect you.

When the Treebor is weakened, we need to wait until it gets distracted and drops its guard. Then we can finish it off. At the right moment, give the command to Clover. His final blow will be precise and merciful, sending the beast to the beginning of the cycle.

Is your heart ready?
Ask me. Child of Sarn. But be quick, the beast won't wait forever.
